pr_title: Fix IndexOutOfRangeException when an added/removed attribute spans a buffer size boundary
pr_body:
**NOTE: I'm not actually proposing this for servicing right now, because it doesn't look like there would be a major benefit from including it in RC1, and including it in RC2 would be perfectly sufficient. However I'm writing up the ask mode template anyway just in case people disagree.**

Extremely rarely, component rendering could cause IndexOutOfRangeException.

## Description

If a component rendered a very specific number of frames, and then updated to render exactly one more frame, and that new frame was an attribute, and it was the last frame in the component, the diffing system would throw `IndexOutOfRangeException`. This was due to a bug in checking whether there are more attributes to process.

Fixes #49192

## Customer Impact

Fairly low, because it's really hard to reproduce this, even if you're doing so on purpose. However, total correctness of the Blazor renderer is a high priority for us, and we do not want any edge cases where it can fail.

In the event that the issue does occur, it would behave like an unhandled exception from application code:

 * For Blazor WebAssembly, the yellow error bar would appear, but the app would continue running
 * For Blazor Server, the current user's circuit would be terminated, but other server activity would be unaffected
 * For Blazor WebView, the unhandled exception callback would run

## Regression?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

[If yes, specify the version the behavior has regressed from]

## Risk

- [ ] High
- [ ] Medium
- [x] Low

Low because the code change is small enough (4 lines) to reason clearly that it only makes a difference in the case where it would have failed before. The updated boundary condition is simple to understand.

- [x] Manual (required)
- [x] Automated

issue_context.body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing issues

### Describe the bug

I have been able to reliably reproduce an issue where RenderTreeDiffBuilder crashes with an IndexOutOfRangeException.

It appears that the order of attributes, as well as the number of nodes and components matter. Any change to the order, attributes, or components make the issue disappear.

The issue appears when using a nullable string, set to null and using it for an input element value attribute.

From my research, it appears similar (possibly the same root cause) to another issue that was closed for incomplete submission: #44542

### Expected Behavior

It appears that a combinaison of attributes and elements make this bug appear.
The expected behavior is for rendering to complete and for the input to have an empty value when the backing variable is null.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Clone the repro project : https://github.com/mat128/blazorwasm_rendertreediffbuilder
2. Execute `dotnet run`
3. Open http://localhost:5121/ in any browser

comments:
Thanks very much for reporting this, @mat128!

I've tracked this down to a framework issue, with a fix in the PR https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/50110

As you're aware, this issue only surfaces in extremely rare scenarios - you have to render a very specific number of frames, then cause a UI change that adds precisely one more attribute. And it has to be the very last attribute in the component. So, it's very easy to work around, just by adding or removing any other content in your component so the "very specific number" criteria is no longer met. Nonetheless, correctness inside the renderer is very important to us, so we are definitely fixing this right away!

review_comments: Both of these new unit tests do fail with `IndexOutOfRangeException` without the fix, and of course pass with the fix.
